now.headline: Money gets one seat. The other five are for making something strange.
now.situation: Floating, pivoting back to making money via art. Shopify shows 0 orders and $0 ever (17 products, 228 sessions in 90 days, 5 carts started, none finished); $2,265 of signed prints sit in archived listings; real sales may live on pay.the37thmove.com. Round 2 re-judges round 1's 24 candidates under a new rule: one path floats around money, five are free of it.
now.question: Is there a painting on an easel right now, and has anyone ever paid you for one? Stop Me depends on both and I can see neither.

paths.title: Stop Me: the buyer decides when it's done
paths.why: Price climbs as the painting gets made; whoever buys freezes it as found. One real sale, no traffic needed.
paths.firstMove: In tabula-rosetta, on a new branch work/stop-me, build work/stop-me/index.html, one self-contained page: a photo slot for the canvas, four stages (ground 370, underpainting 740, halfway 1110, resolved 1480 USD), a live price that only moves up, a Buy placeholder. Write work/stop-me/RULES.md: a purchase ends the painting that day, signed as found, shipped with a studio card naming the stage; no stage sells before its photo exists. Publish nothing. Then draft, for my approval, the Shopify product 'Stop Me, Painting No. 1' and a note to past collectors.
paths.doubt: One sale proves one buyer, not a market. It needs a painting actually in progress and someone who already wants to own it, and I can see neither.

paths.title: Dreamachine sigil: symmetry order is the Hz
paths.why: A sigil cut into a spinning card cylinder; its fold symmetry sets the flicker rate. A perception tool you build in an afternoon.
paths.firstMove: In tabula-rosetta create studio/dreamachine/make_template.py (no deploys, no store writes). Output print-ready SVG and PDF for a card cylinder: an A4-landscape strip (29.7 cm, glue tab included), about 9.3 cm across, with N identical sigil cutouts evenly spaced. At 78 rpm the flicker is N x 1.3 Hz, so emit N = 7, 8 and 9 (9.1, 10.4, 11.7 Hz). Draw the sigil in straight strokes on a hex lattice so it cuts clean. Print the Hz table and a photosensitive-epilepsy warning on the sheet. Bench test: 78 rpm turntable, small LED inside, eyes closed.
paths.doubt: Flicker at 8 to 13 Hz can trigger seizures in photosensitive people. The warning is a floor, not a fix, and I cannot tell you how it feels: you have to spin one.

paths.title: Funerals for dead websites
paths.why: Software has no funerals. Sell an epitaph, a sigil seal and a tombstone for dead projects. Your own Vercel graveyard is the demo.
paths.firstMove: In tabula-rosetta create studio/necropolis/index.html, one file, no deploy. Read docs/DEPLOY.md and make one tombstone each for project-f8yrf, workspace (whose whole content is the word probe), vite-react, playground2.55, tonic-quantum-leap, and one family stone for the-37-th-move 1.4 to 1.8. Each stone: name, last-deploy date, one dry cause of death, and a seal: the name's letters on a 37-node hex lattice drawn as one stroke. Exclude kurts-* and anything marked keep. Delete and archive nothing. Add a Bury yours link to pay.the37thmove.com.
paths.doubt: Funny for an afternoon. Whether anyone would pay to bury a project is untested, and the list of dead projects comes from a doc that may be out of date.

paths.title: Sigil Gun becomes an actual gun
paths.why: A handheld that prints a sigil sticker from any typed wish. The print line becomes a tool, and the glyph becomes a verb.
paths.firstMove: In tabula-rosetta, build work/sigil-gun-label/index.html: type a wish, collapse its letters into one angular illegible glyph (Spare's method, no mandala), render it 1-bit at 384px wide for a 48mm thermal sticker at 203dpi. Save PNGs. If you own or buy a mini thermal sticker printer (Phomemo-class, roughly $30 to $80), print 10, stick them up and photograph the results. Borrow glyph code from the 137-cipher Vercel project if useful. No store writes, no deploys.
paths.doubt: Everything rides on the glyph generator being good; a bad one is a toy. Do the screen version first and buy the printer only if the glyphs earn it.

paths.title: Strike the Stargate files into sigils
paths.why: Declassified remote-viewing files redacted to one surviving sentence, struck into a glyph. Zine plus prints from a public-domain source.
paths.firstMove: Download one declassified Star Gate remote-viewing session PDF yourself from the CIA reading room (this sandbox cannot reach cia.gov) into work/stargate/source.pdf. Call adobe_mandatory_init, run pdf_ocr then pdf_to_markdown. Write one intent sentence; those words survive. Redact every other word with pdf_page_organize (permanent, so on a copy). Apply Spare's letter-strike to the survivors for the glyph. Finish with pdf_to_image previews for a 12-page zine. Stop at previews: no store writes.
paths.doubt: Redaction art has a long lineage; the sigil strike is the new part. I have not tested whether the Adobe tools cope with a scanned 40-page file, and you must download the PDF yourself.

paths.title: Channel 37: a dome show on the dark frequency
paths.why: US TV channel 37 has reportedly been kept dark since 1963 so astronomers can listen. A dome piece on the empty channel, under your number.
paths.firstMove: In tabula-rosetta, prototype prototypes/channel-37-dome with Three.js: a Platonic-solid and 4D-projection piece seen through a fisheye dome camera, on a 10-minute timeline that collapses a rotating tesseract to one line while band hiss drifts in and out. Export a 4096px fisheye test frame and a browser dome preview. First, check the channel-37 claim yourself: it is the hook, and I could not open the source.
paths.doubt: The channel-37 fact comes from memory and one unopened search result: verify it before building on it. Dome shows are a slow, niche market, and I do not know your relationship to the number.

bench.title: 37 Moves: patrons buy a turn, not a print
bench.why: 37 seats at $1,370; each patron buys one irreversible move on a Pink TV board.
bench.held: The bigger money bet. Needs 37 buyers you may not have; Stop Me needs one.

bench.title: Three Shadows: a tarot spread as one object
bench.why: One 3D object casts Past, Present and Future as three sigil shadows.
bench.held: Strong and strange. Held back only because three collisions was too many.

bench.title: Room portraits: ask the room, get testimony
bench.why: Strangers send room tone; you return audio stems and a printed testimony.
bench.held: Round 1's wildcard. Channel 37 fits the brand better; bring this back for stranger.

bench.title: A station on twelve sets only
bench.why: Pink TV's rarest station lives on 12 numbered pink receivers.
bench.held: Shelved for round 3 as a wildcard; needs about $200 of parts.

bench.title: Rent the dark paintings to cameras
bench.why: Film and TV rent pre-cleared art at about 15% of retail. A revenue channel that needs no audience.
bench.held: Runner-up. The Dopesick figures came from a snippet I could not open.

bench.title: A Haunting, billed monthly
bench.why: The console becomes an entity that files a monthly dossier on its owner.
bench.held: Recurring revenue, but wants an audience first.

bench.title: A tape that is the only key to the hidden site
bench.why: An edition of 137 VHS tapes whose audio unlocks a hidden station.
bench.held: Needs a dubbing quote before it is a path.

bench.title: Nine signed prints, each sale raises the next
bench.why: $2,265 of signed prints sit in archived listings while the live variants show 0.
bench.held: The stock fact is real and goes in the headline; the rising price is the gimmick.

bench.title: Audit the inbox for everyone who ever paid
bench.why: Past payers are the warmest buyers.
bench.held: Folded into Stop Me and 37 Moves as their first move.

bench.title: Channel 37: a dome show on the empty frequency
bench.why: US TV channel 37 is kept dark for radio astronomy. A dome show on the dark channel.
bench.held: Money 1. The channel-37 fact is the real gift: it is the brand's own number.
